# Intake: Audit-runner pi calls crash with `Connection error.` from stale-ctx extension exceptions

## Problem statement

Audit-runner `pi` subprocesses crash mid-call and the runner records
`provider_error: Connection error.` because pi extensions loaded into the audit
session throw on a **stale `ExtensionContext`** after pi replaces or reloads the
session. The **fatal uncaught exception** is thrown by the ContextHub-owned
`worklog` recovery extension (`register-recovery.ts`, `_notifyFn` →
`ctx.ui.notify`), not by `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. Two
SorraAgents-owned extensions (`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals`)
throw the *same* stale-ctx error but pi catches those and prints them as
(non-fatal) `Extension error (...)` lines. This blocks audits and therefore the
ship final-validation gate (exit 12).

## Users

- **Release manager** — needs audits to complete so `dev` → `main` is not blocked
  by spurious provider failures.
  - *As a release manager, I want an audit pi call to return a genuine verdict
    even after an extension-triggered session replacement, so the release gate
    is not blocked by an infrastructure crash.*
- **Audit operator** — needs `provider_error` entries in the debug corpus to
  reflect real provider faults, not extension crashes.
  - *As an audit operator, I want the audit debug log to distinguish a real
    provider fault from an extension exception, so I can triage correctly.*
- **Pi extension maintainer** — needs extensions to fail safe when the session
  they were registered against is replaced.
  - *As a maintainer, I want my extension's async callbacks to no-op when the
    captured ctx is invalid, so a session swap cannot crash an unrelated run.*

## Existing state (evidence)

The failure was captured for the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (now deleted).
The debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
(`context=parent`) records:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`,
  `elapsed_seconds: ~713`.
- `raw_stderr` contains one `Extension error
  (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This
  extension ctx is stale ...` line, one identical line for
  `proxy-sse-signals`, and then the **fatal, uncaught** trace:

  ```
  Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. ...
      at ExtensionRunner.assertActive (...)
      at get ui (...)
      at _notifyFn (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:71:41)
      at _notifyRetryAttempt (.../register-recovery.ts:549:5)
      at triggerInvisibleContinue (.../register-recovery.ts:391:7)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (...)
  Node.js v22.22.1
  ```

  The trailing `Node.js v22.22.1` banner shows the pi process **crashed**; the
  audit runner then surfaced `Connection error.` from the pi JSON stream.

Corpus scan across every `reason=provider_error` entry
(`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl`) shows **all** non-empty
`raw_stderr` provider errors carry the `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx stack;
some also carry the `proxy-compaction-bridge` / `proxy-sse-signals`
`Extension error` lines (non-fatal, caught by pi).

Root cause of each stale access:

- `ContextHub .../register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` is assigned a closure over
  the *handler's* `ctx` (`_notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(...)`,
  lines ~84/87/212) and is later invoked from the async retry loop
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`). If the session was replaced/reloaded in
  between, `ctx.ui` throws — and because the call originates in a timer/async
  callback, pi never catches it and the process dies.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — both `after_provider_response`
  and `context` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` on the event
  ctx; a stale ctx throws.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — `turn_start` captures `ctx.ui` as
  `statusUi`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls `statusUi.setStatus(...)`
  on the stale UI handle.

`pi` supports `--no-extensions` / `-ne` (disables extension discovery), alongside
the `--no-context-files --no-skills` flags the audit runner already adds to
`_call_pi`. Audit prompts are read-only and fully self-contained, so they do not
depend on extensions.

## Desired change

1. **Unblock audit calls (SorraAgents-owned):** stop loading interactive/UI
   extensions in audit-runner pi subprocesses — add `--no-extensions` to the
   `_call_pi` command (mirroring the existing context-reduction flags).
2. **Harden the SorraAgents-owned extensions:** make `proxy-compaction-bridge`
   and `proxy-sse-signals` fail safe on a stale/replaced ctx — never call
   `ctx.ui`/`ctx.sessionManager` on an invalidated ctx (guard, re-capture from a
   fresh handler, or no-op/passthrough).
3. **Fatal crash (cross-repo handoff — delivered):** the ContextHub
   `worklog` recovery-extension stale-ctx crash is handed off to
   **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (`Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale
   ExtensionContext after session replacement (_notifyFn)`), which is not edited
   from this SorraAgents work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No extension crash on audit calls:** the audit runner's `_call_pi` command
   excludes extension discovery (`--no-extensions`). Verified by a unit test
   asserting the constructed command (both tool-enabled and tool-disabled paths).
2. **Stale-ctx-safe SorraAgents extensions:** `proxy-compaction-bridge` and
   `proxy-sse-signals` no-op (context passthrough / status unchanged) when their
   handler or async callback observes an invalidated `ctx`, never throwing.
   Verified by `node:test` unit tests injecting a stale-ctx stub.
3. **Re-audit completes genuinely:** a re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB (or an
   equivalent audit pi call that triggers a session replacement) completes with a
   genuine verdict (`met`/`partial`/`adjusted`) and the debug entry's `reason` is
   not `provider_error` with `Connection error.` attributable to an extension
   exception.
4. **Regression tests:** a stale/replaced-session-ctx regression test exists for
   both `pi-client` extensions (Node unit tests) and a Python test asserts the
   audit `_call_pi` command includes `--no-extensions`; the tests fail against
   the pre-fix code.
5. **Docs + full suite:** `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` (F6) are updated to reflect the corrected
   attribution/fix; all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is
   updated; and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo boundary:** the fatal crash is in
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (separate repo and `WL-` worklog). It is
  **not** edited from this item; the fix is tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B.
- **Do not regress** the compaction-bridge wire contract
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) or the dispatch reshape semantics/tests.
- **Do not weaken fail-closed audit behaviour**; the audit runner must still
  return `unmet`/`partial` on genuine provider errors, not mask them.
- `--no-extensions` affects all discovered extensions in audit calls only; the
  interactive TUI extension behaviour (compaction mirroring, status line,
  recovery) must remain unchanged.
- `wl`-tracked, test-first, build → test → commit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` builds the pi command
  (~L3648); add `--no-extensions`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — command-flag tests (~L267–304);
  add the `--no-extensions` assertion.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — guard/re-bind the session id
  used by `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js` — pure core (no ctx
  access); keep behaviour, extend tests only.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — guard the captured `statusUi` used by
  the capturing-fetch callback.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` — stale-ctx regression coverage.
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`, `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` —
  documentation/correction.
- *(cross-repo, tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B)*
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`.

## Related work (manual)

- **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** — `[test-failure] getCompletedOrInReviewItems ...`
  (`discovered-from`; the audit that failed with this signature; now deleted).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for
  child audits in the final-validation gate (records the same failure as the
  motivation for removing manual interruptions).
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — RCA: Audit Pipeline Reliability
  (`docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`); F6 documents the 9 `provider_error`
  entries (incl. `Connection error.`) and their conflation with parse failures.
- **SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0** — origin of `proxy-compaction-bridge` (wire contract
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- **SA-0MSHAKSEA001LQ6T** — origin of `proxy-sse-signals`.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — audit context reduction
  (`--no-context-files --no-skills`); precedent for adding a loader flag to
  `_call_pi`.
- **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (ContextHub) — handoff item for the fatal
  `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/cross-repo).** Debug-log evidence shows the *fatal* uncaught
  exception is thrown by the ContextHub-owned `worklog` extension
  (`register-recovery.ts`), not `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. How should
  this item be scoped?
  - Answer (producer): **(c) analysis/handoff** — do not edit ContextHub from this
    item; **create a `WL-` item** for the fatal `register-recovery` crash, and do
    the SorraAgents-side extensions/audit fixes + tests here.
  - Evidence: created **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** in ContextHub; SorraAgents-side
    work captured in the ACs above (consistent with Q3 = (a), which names tests
    for the `pi-client` extensions and the audit `--no-extensions` command).
- **Q2 (audit extension policy).** Is disabling extension discovery for
  audit-runner pi calls (`pi ... --no-extensions`, alongside
  `--no-context-files --no-skills`) acceptable?
  - Answer (producer): **n/a** — not separately decided; Q3(a) explicitly names
    the `--no-extensions` command assertion, so it is in scope (AC1/AC4).
- **Q3 (regression-test surface).** Where should the stale-ctx regression test
  live?
  - Answer (producer): **(a)** Node unit tests for both `pi-client` extensions
    plus a Python test asserting the audit pi command includes `--no-extensions`.
  - Recorded as AC4.
data.title: Audit-runner pi calls crash with 'Connection error.' from stale-ctx extension exceptions after session replacement

discovered-from: SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` pushes with a hard-coded 120 s timeout:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: Command '['git', 'push', ...]' timed out after 120 seconds
```

But the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` runs the **full test suite** for pushes
targeting `refs/heads/dev|main` (`run_tests.py --scope full`). Any project whose
full suite takes longer than 120 s therefore cannot complete `implement.py
finish`: the commit succeeds, but the push is killed, the worktree is removed,
and the item is left `open` (safety reset) with the commit stranded on the
feature branch. Observed for both the companion cleanup (commit e36dd153) and
the F7 verification (commit 649ff913), each requiring a manual background push.

Worse, killing the `git push` does not kill the pre-push hook's child
`run_tests.py`: orphaned hook processes survived and deadlocked a subsequent
push attempt (both waiting on the same cache lock). Manual `kill` of the
orphaned hooks was required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** The `finish` push timeout is configurable and defaults to a value that
  accommodates the repo's pre-push gate (e.g. reuse `timeoutPerCommand` from
  `.pi/test-config.json`, currently 1500 s) rather than a fixed 120 s.
  *Verification:* a test proves a slow pre-push hook no longer times out.
- **AC2** On push timeout, `finish` terminates the spawned hook children (process
  group kill), leaving no orphaned `run_tests.py`/hook processes.
  *Verification:* a test simulating a slow hook asserts no surviving child.
- **AC3** A push timeout leaves recoverable state: the commit hash and the
  feature branch are reported, and the work item is not silently reset without
  an actionable message.
  *Verification:* a test asserts the finish report names the commit hash and
  branch and that a manual-push comment is posted on timeout.
- **AC4** Full suite passes; docs (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) describe the timeout behaviour.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` push call, its hard-coded
  `timeout=120` in `git_push_to_dev()`, and the existing `_resolve_test_timeout()`
  helper (reads `.pi/test-config.json`) to reuse for the configurable timeout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `timeoutPerCommand` config reader (reuse).
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — new tests for AC1/AC2/AC3 (slow-hook
  timeout, process-group kill, recoverable-state reporting).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the timeout contract.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — implementation-reference detail for
  the timeout behaviour.

## Plan

Single-item bug fix (effort XS / risk Low) — no child work items required.
Implementation order: (1) make the push timeout configurable via the existing
`_resolve_test_timeout()` reader; (2) spawn the push in its own process group
and kill the group on timeout; (3) surface commit hash + branch + manual-push
comment on timeout; (4) add tests then docs. Test-first per AC verification.
data.title: implement.py finish push times out (120s) before the pre-push full-suite gate completes

# audit_runner failure-restore reuses an invalid pre-audit status/stage combo, leaving items unrecoverable

## Problem statement

When an audit ends in an infrastructure-failure / fallback-tainted "Ready to close: No" verdict, `audit_runner.py` restores the captured pre-audit `status`+`stage` verbatim. If that captured combination is already invalid (which happens when an item was imported/refiled with status and stage set independently), every restore attempt is rejected by `wl` and the item is left in an unresolved, inconsistent state.

Observed during the audit of SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD on 2026-09-26 (session herdr-1790437388-2668941-15858, log `/home/rgardler/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD-20260926-173301.log`):

- Phase 1 parent screening hit audit-concurrency starvation → unparseable → infra-fallback `partial` for all ACs.
- `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` correctly chose the restore branch, building `wl update <id> --status blocked --stage in_review`.
- The captured combo was invalid (`blocked` is not compatible with `in_review`), so all 3 attempts failed.
- The runner printed "the item's lifecycle is unresolved" and exited non-zero.

The item's pre-audit status was already invalid (`in-progress`/`in_review`; `wl` allows stage `in_review` only with status `completed`).

## Root cause

`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) and `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) only substitute a safe stage when `safe_stage` is falsy (i.e. `ctx.original_stage` was never captured). A present-but-invalid captured combo is used as-is, so the restore cannot succeed and the item is stranded.

## Desired change

Before applying a restore (or a "No" demotion), validate the intended `(status, stage)` pair against `wl`'s allowed combinations and coerce to the nearest valid pair (e.g. keep the status but fall back to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`/`idea` for non-completed statuses), or retry with a stage-agnostic update. Never leave an item in an invalid combination after the runner exits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit `(status, stage)` combination is invalid, the failure/restore path applies a valid, consistent state instead of failing all attempts, and the runner never leaves the item in an invalid combination.
2. A regression test covers restoring an item whose captured combo is invalid (e.g. `blocked`/`in_review`) and asserts a valid terminal state is reached.
3. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix must not alter the semantic intent of the restore: preserve the captured status (e.g. `blocked` stays `blocked`) and only coerce the stage when the combination is invalid.
- The valid status/stage mapping is defined in `config.js` (`statusStageCompatibility`):
  - `open` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `in-progress` → `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `input_needed` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `blocked` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `completed` → `in_review`, `done`
  - `deleted` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `done`
- The fix should be self-contained in the audit runner's restore logic; no changes to `wl` itself.

## Existing state

Two locations apply the restore:
1. `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) — standalone restore after verification failure.
2. `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) — primary restore path in the verdict-driven transition.

Both follow the same pattern:
```python
safe_status = ctx.original_status or "open"
safe_stage = ctx.original_stage
if not safe_stage:
    safe_stage = "in_review" if safe_status == "completed" else "plan_complete"
```

This only handles the case where `original_stage` was never captured. When `original_stage` exists but is incompatible with `original_status`, the combo is invalid and rejected by `wl`.

## Desired change (implementation)

Introduce a helper function `_coerce_valid_status_stage(status, stage)` that:
1. Validates the `(status, stage)` pair against the `statusStageCompatibility` map.
2. Returns `(status, stage)` unchanged if valid.
3. If invalid, keeps the captured status but falls back to a valid stage:
   - For non-`completed` statuses: `plan_complete` (the closest "work in progress" stage).
   - For `completed`: `in_review`.
4. Logs a warning when coercion occurs, so operators know the original state was non-standard.

Apply this helper in both `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` and `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` before building the `wl update` command.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Coercion changes the restored state slightly.** The stage may shift (e.g. `in_review` → `plan_complete` for a `blocked` item). This is intentional and safer than leaving the item unrecoverable. Operators should note the warning message.
- **The `statusStageCompatibility` mapping lives in ContextHub's `config.js`, not SorraAgents.** The audit runner must not import from ContextHub. Valid combos should be inlined in `audit_runner.py` (or sourced from a shared constant in `skill/shared/`). This is a deliberate isolation choice.
- **Scope creep risk:** Only fix the restore path — do not address all status/stage issues in the runner (e.g. the "No" demotion path or the "Yes" advance path, which already produce valid combos). Source: explicit scope from the original report.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** — "Audit runner demotes in_review item to open/plan_complete on infrastructure-failure fallback verdicts" — the prior fix that added the `fallback_tainted` flag and restore path. This issue is a follow-up: the restore itself fails when the captured combo is invalid.
- **SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD** — the item that exposed the bug during audit.
- **SA-0MS99053T001ED0C** — "find-related and refactor skills still flip status to completed via StatusLifecycle" — related StatusLifecycle correctness issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** When coercing an invalid `(status, stage)` pair, should we preserve the captured status or also attempt to adjust the status? — **Answer (Map):** Preserve the captured status and only coerce the stage. The status carries the item's operational state (blocked/in-progress/open) which should not be silently altered. Source: analysis of the `statusStageCompatibility` mapping.
- **Q2:** Should the coercion helper be placed in `audit_runner.py` or shared (`status_lifecycle.py`)? — **Answer (Map):** Place it in `audit_runner.py` for now; if `status_lifecycle.py` needs the same logic (e.g. for general wl validation), refactor to shared later. Source: current usage is audit-runner-specific.
- **Q3:** What log level should coercion warnings use? — **Answer (Map):** `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` (consistent with existing error paths in the runner). Source: audit_runner.py convention.
data.title: audit_runner failure-restore reuses an invalid pre-audit status/stage combo, leaving items unrecoverable

# Audit runner: re-auditing an in_review child demotes it and can cascade a parent block

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high

## Problem statement

A parent audit can silently demote children that were already `completed` /
`in_review` (and therefore exempt from the parent's child-stage and
child-verdict blocking checks) and then fail its own closure against those
demoted stages — reporting `Ready to close: No` even when every parent
acceptance criterion is `met`. On 2026-09-27, auditing
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` re-screened three children whose content had changed
because the parent's commit touched files they own; each received a persisted
`Ready to close: No` child audit and was demoted (F2 →
`open`/`plan_complete`, F3 → `blocked`/`plan_complete`, F6 →
`blocked`/`plan_complete`). The parent's own verdict became `No` purely
because those children were no longer exempt, despite all six parent ACs
being `met`.

## Users and user stories

- **Audit operator** — As an audit operator, I want a parent audit to evaluate
  its own closure against the children's status as it was when the audit
  started, so an otherwise-complete parent is reported `Yes` even if a child
  is re-screened as a side effect.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want a parent audit to never
  demote a completed/`in_review` child unless that child was deliberately,
  independently audited as not-ready, so a parent run cannot silently push
  completed work back into the actionable queue and cascade `blocked` states
  through the dependency chain.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want verdicts driven only by
  unverifiable/historical or out-of-manifest ACs to be distinguishable from
  genuine code gaps, so a read-only re-audit does not downgrade an
  already-reviewed child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Snapshot/exception semantics:** A children snapshot is taken at
   parent-audit start, and the parent's closure decision exempts every child
   that was in `in_review`/`done` (or otherwise exempt) at that point — even
   if the child's stage changed during the parent run. A parent whose own ACs
   are all `met`/`adjusted` is not blocked by children that were exempt at
   audit start.
2. **No side-effect demotion:** A child audit that is triggered as a side
   effect of a parent audit (the `--audit-children` cascade or the
   content-changed auto re-screen) does not change the child's lifecycle
   (`status`/`stage`) when the child was `in_review`/`done` before the parent
   run. Only a child explicitly and independently audited as not-ready may be
   demoted.
3. **No regression to genuine blocking:** A child that is in a pre-review
   stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) or that is independently
   audited and genuinely not-ready still blocks the parent's closure. The
   existing exemption rules and the parent-first pass-through are preserved.
4. **Verdict fidelity:** ACs that are unverifiable in a read-only audit
   (historical/execution-dependent properties, or verification files outside
   the child's file-scope manifest) do not silently become blocking `partial`
   verdicts that demote an otherwise-complete item; either they are handled by
   the snapshot/no-demotion fix or they carry a distinct non-blocking
   classification.
5. **Regression test:** An automated test pins acceptance criterion 1 and 2:
   a parent audit over an `in_review` child whose only failing AC is
   unverifiable yields parent `Ready to close: Yes` and leaves the child at
   `completed`/`in_review` (or, if the chosen approach preserves the child
   stage via snapshot instead, the test asserts the parent `Yes` and the
   pre-audit child stage).
6. **Documentation:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the child-exemption snapshot
   / no-side-effect-demotion contract, including how `--audit-children` and
   the content-changed re-screen interact with it. All related documentation is
   updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The audit remains **read-only** except the authorized persistence and
  verdict-driven status lifecycle; the fix must not add new state mutations.
- Must not weaken genuine blocking: a truly not-ready, independently audited
  child must still block its parent.
- Must preserve the existing `in_review`/`done` exemption, `inherited_pass`
  pass-through, and content-fingerprint freshness/reuse semantics.
- Keep the change surgical; prefer extracting shared logic over duplicating
  stage/verdict logic between `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` and
  `_build_issue_json`.
- Any change to child lifecycle must be consistent between the markdown
  report path (`_assemble_issue_report`) and the JSON path
  (`_build_issue_json`).

## Existing state

- `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` and `_build_issue_json()` exempt children
  whose **current** `stage` is `in_review` (plus `status=completed` +
  `stage=done`, deleted, and `inherited_pass`). The exemption is evaluated at
  report-assembly time, against whatever stage the child holds *after* the
  parent run.
- The `--audit-children` cascade auto-triggers
  `audit_runner.py issue <child> --force`; that child run applies its own
  terminal lifecycle (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`): a genuine `No` verdict
  transitions the child to `open`/`plan_complete` (and `wl` dependency state
  can surface it as `blocked`). The parent then evaluates its exemption
  against the demoted child stage and blocks.
- In the default parent-first flow, children whose content-fingerprint
  changed are re-screened and their audits persisted via
  `_persist_child_audit()`, which does not itself change the child stage — so
  the observed demotion originates in the cascade re-audit path.
- Unverifiable ACs (e.g. "the tests fail for behavioural reasons *before*
  F3–F5 land", or a file outside the child's file-scope manifest) fall to
  `partial`, a blocking verdict, which drives the child `No` and the
  subsequent demotion.

## Desired change

Make a parent audit non-destructive to already-exempt children and evaluate
the parent's closure against the child-exemption status captured at audit
start. Candidate mechanisms (the implementer may choose any that satisfies all
ACs, or a combination):

- **Snapshot exempt children at audit start** and evaluate the parent's
  closure against the snapshot rather than the post-re-audit stages
  (satisfies AC1).
- **Preserve a child's prior terminal stage** when a cascade-triggered child
  audit's verdict is driven only by unverifiable / out-of-manifest ACs
  (satisfies AC2, AC4).
- **Make child re-audit opt-in** so the default parent audit never mutates
  child lifecycle (satisfies AC2, complements AC1).
- **Introduce a distinct `unverifiable` verdict** for
  historical/execution-dependent ACs so they do not silently become blocking
  `partial` (satisfies AC4).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()`,
  `_build_issue_json()`, `_phase_children()` (cascade / auto-trigger),
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, `_child_content_changed()`,
  `_persist_child_audit()`, `_assemble_issue_report()`: snapshot exempt
  children at start; suppress side-effect demotion; keep markdown and JSON
  verdict paths consistent.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` — existing exemption/verdict unit tests
  (`test_child_audit_does_not_block_phase1_when_in_review`,
  `test_ready_false_when_child_audit_no`, etc.); add the regression test for
  AC5.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — child inclusion / lifecycle tests
  (e.g. `test_completed_in_review_child_included_in_child_results`); extend
  for the snapshot/exemption behaviour.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle + child-exemption documentation.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — parent-first pass-through and
  `--audit-children` cascade documentation.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the fix needs to suppress or
  gate a lifecycle transition for cascade-triggered child audits.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Over-broad exemption (regression risk):** snapshotting "exempt at start"
  could let a genuinely broken child block-free if the parent started while
  the child was still `in_review`. Mitigation: keep the existing pre-review
  and independent-audit blocking paths intact (AC3) and add explicit tests
  for the pre-review block.
- **Fix only patches the parent decision, not the child demotion:** the child
  still ends up `open`/`blocked`, leaving the release queue inconsistent.
  Mitigation: treat AC1 and AC2 as jointly required, not alternatives.
- **Two divergent verdict paths:** `_build_issue_json()` and
  `_assemble_issue_report()` could drift. Mitigation: extract shared
  exemption/verdict logic and test both paths.
- **Cascade never re-audits genuinely changed children:** if re-audit becomes
  strictly opt-in, a changed child could inherit a stale pass. Mitigation:
  preserve the content-fingerprint gate so changed children are still
  surfaced, just not demoted by a parent-triggered run.
- **Scope creep:** other known audit defects (e.g.
  `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`, `SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2`, `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL`) are
  related but out of scope; record them as linked work items, not scope.

## Evidence

- Parent report (all 6 ACs `met`, verdict `No`):
  `wl audit-show SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 --json`.
- Demoted children: `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` (now `open`/`plan_complete`),
  `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` and `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` (now
  `blocked`/`plan_complete`), updated at `2026-09-27T01:10:42–44Z`.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** (open) — discovered-from: the parent whose audit
  exposed the bug (all parent ACs `met`, verdict `No`).
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** (completed) — "Audit runner has circular dependency
  — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage": introduced the
  `in_review` exemption this bug defeats.
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (open) and **SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2** (open) — related
  `inherited_pass` / pre-review child-stage blocking defects; coordinate to
  avoid conflicting fixes in the same exemption logic.
- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** (completed) — precedence for "restore, never
  demote" on infrastructure-fallback verdicts; a useful pattern for the
  no-side-effect-demotion requirement.
- **SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD**, **SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P** (completed) — Phase 1 child
  AC review / child-verdict reuse and content-fingerprint freshness, which
  determine when a changed child is re-screened.

## Assumptions

- The fix is scope-limited to the `skill/audit` runner; no change to `wl`
  itself is required.
- Preserving the child's pre-audit stage (rather than snapshotting only the
  parent's decision) is the intended reading of AC3 — the implementer selects
  the concrete mechanism that satisfies both AC1 and AC2.
- `--audit-children` remains available for operators who explicitly want a
  full recursive re-audit; an explicit, independent child audit keeps its
  normal lifecycle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed work-item description already
specified the observed behaviour, the evidence (demoted child ids, parent
report), the desired behaviour, and three candidate mitigation shapes. All
related work was resolved by worklog search and repo inspection, so no
operator/producer input was needed. This intake did not ask any questions.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQ9D9I6P007R6VV** – Add create-child mode to triage check_or_create.py for blocking child creation (completed)
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MSPPD6HE0054KO8** – plan/SKILL.md: replace wl list --parent dump with existence check (completed)

## Goal

Fix the runaway triage retry loop in the audit runner's F3 full-suite auto-execution so an audit never hangs and always completes (or fails cleanly).

Discovered while auditing SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X (discovered-from:SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X). Blocks re-audit of that item per operator decision.

## Failure Signature

During `audit_runner.py issue SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X` F3 auto-execution (`_run_tests_via_test_skill`), the runner repeatedly invoked the triage helper for the SAME failing test:

- Work item: SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X
- HEAD: 95184f21c18808564ddb515e8a0edd798537d3d6
- Test name triaged: skill/audit/tests/test_audit_execute.py::TestGateNeverBlocksOnCacheMiss::test_cache_miss_proceeds_to_phase1
- Observed: 170+ `triage.issue.blocking_child` events in ~15 min, each failing `wl dep add SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X SA-0MUMAOPTU009L2MU` (exit 1).
- The runner process consumed ~1s CPU and emitted ~6 KB/min of the same repeating records; it never printed its completion line and never returned. It was killed per the monitored-run abort contract.

## Evidence

- Run log: ~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X-20260929-071920.log
- The repeated pair is:
  - `{"event": "triage.issue.blocking_child", "issueId": "SA-0MUMAOPTU009L2MU", "parentWorkItemId": "SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X", "heuristic": "token_overlap_stacktrace"}` (alternating with `commit_or_ci_url`)
  - `[triage] wl command failed: wl dep add SA-0MUM5UWL4005YH0X SA-0MUMAOPTU009L2MU --json: ... returned non-zero exit status 1.`
- `parse_pytest_failures` (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) returns one record per `FAILED`/`ERROR` summary match (`_RED_SUMMARY_RE`), and `_run_tests_via_test_skill` (skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py) triages every record in an unbounded `for failure in failures:` loop with no dedup and no cap. Under host contention the captured pytest output contained many duplicate/ambiguous summary-shaped lines for one test, producing a huge `failures` list and thus the runaway loop.

## Root Cause (hypothesis)

`_run_tests_via_test_skill` triages N failure records with no de-duplication by test identity and no upper bound. When the parsed output over-produces records for a single failing test (observed under concurrent full-suite runs / shared test semaphore), the triage call count grows without bound and the audit appears hung.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_run_tests_via_test_skill` de-duplicates triage by test identity so `check_or_create` is called at most once per distinct failing test per run.
2. Triage count is bounded (hard cap) and the function always reaches its completion print/return regardless of individual `check_or_create`/`wl dep add` failures.
3. A regression test reproduces the over-production condition (a pytest-output fixture with repeated/ambiguous FAILED summary lines for one test) and asserts a bounded number of `check_or_create` calls.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Goal

Make the pre-push full-suite gate pass for pushes made from a git worktree, so the implement workflow's mandated worktree push path does not require an undocumented override.

## Failure Signature

Pushing to dev from a worktree (.worklog/worktrees/wl-*) fails with:

    pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env
    ERROR: Full test suite failed — pushes to dev/main require a green suite.

The failure is immediate (not a suite run) because run_tests.py refuses to start:

    run_tests: refusing to run the release gate with repository-override env var(s) present: GIT_DIR.

## Root Cause

git exports GIT_DIR to pre-push hooks. From a worktree, GIT_DIR is the worktree admin gitdir (e.g. <main>/.git/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>). .githooks/pre-push invokes run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env, and run_tests.py's release-gate fail-fast (skill/shared/git_sandbox.py REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS) treats any GIT_DIR as a leaked repository override and exits 2. Verified: hook env from a worktree contains GIT_DIR; from the main checkout it does not.

## Impact

Every worktree push to dev/main fails at the gate, blocking the implement skill's Step 9 push. Workaround used for SA-0MUMC6LGE005UQNS: RUN_TESTS_ALLOW_REPO_OVERRIDES=1 (documented override; loud warning; scrub still applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pushing to dev from a worktree passes the pre-push full-suite gate without RUN_TESTS_ALLOW_REPO_OVERRIDES=1.
2. The gate still refuses a genuine leaked GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE (real repository-override leak) as today.
3. Regression test reproduces the hook environment (GIT_DIR set by git for a worktree hook) and asserts the gate runs the suite rather than refusing.
4. Full project test suite passes.

# Isolate `TestPrePushWiring` from ambient hook-bypass variables

## Problem statement

`tests/test_git_identity_guard.py::TestPrePushWiring` runs the real pre-push
hook as a subprocess but builds that subprocess environment with `_env()`,
which scrubs only a fixed list of git **repository-override** variables
(`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, …) — it does **not** scrub `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH`.
When the suite itself is launched under a pre-push hook (where the operator has
set `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` to bypass `wl sync` from a worktree), the variable
is inherited by the pytest process, then by the fake hook. The hook takes its
early `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` exit **before** the identity guard and
`wl sync`, so both wiring tests fail.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** (example user story: *As an agent pushing
  from a worktree, I want `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` to bypass only `wl sync`,
  not to change unrelated test outcomes, so the release gate is trustworthy.*)
- **Release-gate maintainers** (example user story: *As a maintainer, I want the
  pre-push full-suite gate to be deterministic regardless of ambient bypass
  variables, so it cannot poison its own test cache and block every push to
  `dev`.*)
- **Operators/CI** running the suite with hook-bypass variables exported.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_git_identity_guard.py::TestPrePushWiring -q` passes (currently 2 failed).
2. `TestPrePushWiring` explicitly controls every hook-bypass variable relevant to the hook under test — at minimum `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH`, and for defence the other bypass switches the hook reads (`BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP`, `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP`, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP`) — so the ambient environment cannot change the test's behaviour.
3. A regression test asserts the isolation: with `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` present in the parent process environment, `_env()` excludes it and the existing wiring cases still behave correctly.
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically a note in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9 on ambient hook-bypass variables).

## Constraints

- The fix must stay local to the test fixture where practical; do **not** weaken
  the production pre-push hook's documented `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` bypass
  (`.githooks/pre-push`). The defect is test non-isolation, not hook behaviour.
- Use the repo's existing isolation pattern (an explicit, allow-listed scrub in
  `_env()`), consistent with `_OVERRIDE_VARS` and
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`. Do not blanket-clear the whole environment.
- Preserve the existing test intent (fake `wl` marker proves the guard ordering);
  the tests must continue to exercise the real committed hook.
- No change to `run_tests.py` cache semantics is required, but the fix must make
  the cache deterministic under a polluted parent environment.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_git_identity_guard.py` `_env(home)` builds the subprocess env from
  `os.environ`, dropping `_OVERRIDE_VARS` and `WORKLOG_EXPECTED_EMAIL`, and sets
  `HOME`/`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`. It does not drop `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` (v3) reads `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` at the worklog-sync
  stage and exits 0 before the git-identity guard runs. It also reads
  `BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP`, `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP`, and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP`.
- `TestPrePushWiring._setup_hook_repo` already sets `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`,
  `BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP=1`, and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` explicitly, so those switches
  are already deterministic; only `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` leaks through.
- Reproduced on the current checkout:
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_git_identity_guard.py::TestPrePushWiring -q`
  → `2 failed` (`test_mismatched_identity_skips_wl_sync`,
  `test_healthy_identity_runs_wl_sync`); without the variable the tests pass.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` records failures in the test cache keyed by
  git state, so an ambient-polluted run caches these failures and the pre-push
  suite gate can then block all pushes to `dev` (observed blocking
  SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5).

## Desired change

- In `_env()`, scrub the hook-bypass variables relevant to the hook under test —
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` (required) plus the other bypass switches the hook
  reads, which the fixture re-sets explicitly per test — so ambient values never
  reach the hook subprocess.
- Add a regression test (e.g. `test_ambient_hook_bypass_var_is_scrubbed`) that
  pollutes `os.environ` with `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` (via `monkeypatch`) and
  asserts (a) `_env()` omits it and (b) the mismatched-identity case still
  observes `git identity mismatch` and skips `wl sync`.
- Document the ambient hook-bypass isolation gap and its fix in
  `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9 (prevention-layers table / regression coverage).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_git_identity_guard.py` — Add `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` (and sibling bypass switches) to the `_env()` scrub; add the ambient-pollution regression test.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — Read-only reference: the bypass variables and their early-exit ordering that the test must control (no change expected).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — Add the ambient hook-bypass variable note to §9 (prevention layers / regression coverage).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Context only: the cache/gate path that makes the non-isolation consequential (no change expected).

## Related work

- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** (`discovered-from`) — push was blocked by this defect.
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** — restored `wl sync` after the main-checkout git
  identity incident; introduced the guard and `TestPrePushWiring`.
- **SA-0MUMR3QPM002VK7M** — pre-push full-suite gate vs. worktree pushes; same
  hook/gate area and same "gate blocks its own push" failure surface.
- **SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0** — migrate remaining raw-git test helpers to
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox` (the shared scrub helper this fixture mirrors).
- **SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG** — release-gate fail-fast on repository-override vars
  (the existing isolation precedent).

## Risks, assumptions, and scope

- **Assumption:** the operator's ambient `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` is intended to
  skip only `wl sync`; test outcomes must not depend on it. Evidence: hook
  comment `.githooks/pre-push:11` scopes the bypass to worklog sync.
- **Risk (regression):** a blanket "clear all env" fix would break `PATH`/`HOME`
  handling; mitigated by allow-list scrubbing consistent with existing `_env()`
  logic.
- **Risk (hidden siblings):** other tests that run `.githooks/pre-push` may read
  ambient bypass vars; the new regression test names the class of defect but
  scope is limited to `TestPrePushWiring` (a broader sweep, if needed, is
  linked — not in scope).
- **Scope-creep guard:** changes to the production hook's bypass semantics and
  to `run_tests.py` cache behaviour are **out of scope**; record as separate
  work items if discovered.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (problem,
  reproduction, impact, ACs) was sufficient to draft this brief without an
  interview, per the intake interview guidance ("skip the interview when the
  seed context suffices to draft a clear brief").
- Reproduction confirmed by the agent on the current checkout:
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_git_identity_guard.py::TestPrePushWiring -q`
  → `2 failed in 0.16s`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQJIL0HS0035BIZ** – Implement: explicit no-push-to-dev in implement-single (completed)
- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** – [test-failure] test_audit_skill_doc.py::TestAuditSkillWorkItemIdDetection::test_scan_match_branch_structure — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35** – Enable the context-budget pre-push gate across all framework projects (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, acceptance, bash, behave, behaviour (+78 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, asserts, bash, behave (+76 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, bash, behave, behaviour (+66 more)

## Goal

Eliminate the ship release failure mode where `in_review` items with a stale
audit verdict (`readyToClose=false` from an out-of-date audit) hard-block the
release at the Step 2 audit gate (exit 6) before the staleness-aware
final-validation sweep (Step 3.7) can remediate them — and make the
release-time audit remediation path cost-bounded so a large backlog of
missing/stale audits cannot exhaust the release's time/slot budget.

## Reported symptom (root cause)

An agent releasing a project with ~20 unaudited/stale `in_review` items saw the
release die at Step 2. Re-running `audit_runner.py issue <id>` took >20 min per
item (Phase 1 parent screening alone 1160s; proxy `cheap` mode serialises audit
concurrency to 1). The gate's per-item remediation timeout is 600s, so every
remediation attempt reported "remediation runner failed — blocking". The
smarter staleness-aware sweep never ran because Step 2 blocked first.

## Root causes (confirmed by code inspection)

1. `check-audit-gate.js` `getAuditStatus()` treats any `readyToClose=false` as a
   genuine verdict → immediate block (exit 6). It has no staleness check, while
   `check-final-validation.js` (`classifyAudit`) does. Step 2 runs first.
2. `getCandidateItems()` does not project `updatedAt`, so Step 2 cannot even
   evaluate staleness.
3. The per-item remediation timeout is hardcoded at 600000 ms in both gates,
   with no env override and no total budget.
4. Audit re-runs happen inside the release gate, serially (by design — parallel
   spawns caused the SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL fan-out), so a backlog takes hours.

## Scope

- In scope: `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`,
  `check-final-validation.js`, `run-release.js`, a new shared freshness module,
  ship docs/tests.
- Out of scope: changing the audit runner's own concurrency/slot semantics
  (covered by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF), and the herdr dispatcher idle gate.

## Children

1. SA-… Step-2 audit gate shares staleness logic with final validation (critical).
2. SA-… Bound remediation cost + actionable offline refresh guidance (high).
3. SA-… Pre-flight audit refresh so release gating never runs long re-audits (high).
4. SA-… Consume persisted audit content fingerprint for staleness (medium).
5. SA-… Distinguish audit-infra failure from genuine verdict + narrow bypass (medium).

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

1. A stale `readyToClose=false` audit on a top-level `in_review` item does NOT
   hard-block at Step 2; it is either remediated or deferred to Step 3.7.
2. A fresh genuine `readyToClose=false` verdict still blocks the release.
3. A release with many missing/stale audits cannot exceed a bounded remediation
   budget, and fails with an actionable message when the budget is exhausted.
4. No regression: parent-coverage semantics, child scope resolution, producer
   review gating, and existing tests all pass.
5. Full project test suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship skill: eliminate stale-audit false blocks and bound release-time audit cost

data.description:
## Goal

Make the Step 2 audit gate (`checkAuditReadyToClose`, exit 6) staleness-aware so
a stale `readyToClose=false` verdict no longer hard-blocks the release before the
already staleness-aware Step 3.7 final-validation sweep can remediate it.

## Why

`check-final-validation.js` `classifyAudit()` puts staleness ahead of the verdict
(a stale "not ready to close" is remediated). `check-audit-gate.js`
`getAuditStatus()` does not, and Step 2 runs first (exit 6), so the release dies
before the smarter gate runs. `getCandidateItems()` also omits `updatedAt`, so
Step 2 cannot compute staleness at all.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared module (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js`) owns
   `parseIsoUtc`, `isAuditStale`, `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`,
   `AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`; both `check-audit-gate.js` and
   `check-final-validation.js` import from it with no import cycle.
2. `getCandidateItems()` / `getTopLevelCandidateItems()` project `updatedAt`.
3. `getAuditStatus()` returns explicit `passing` / `stale` / `transient` /
   `failing` / missing classification. A stale (audit predates item update)
   `readyToClose=false` audit is classified stale and non-blocking; a fresh
   genuine `readyToClose=false` stays blocking.
4. `checkAuditReadyToClose()` auto-remediates stale audits via the existing
   conservative path instead of blocking immediately; only a still-failing
   result after remediation blocks.
5. `resolveChildScope()` coverage still requires a *passing* parent audit
   (`readyToClose===true`) — a stale/failing parent must NOT cover children.
6. Unit tests cover: stale Step-2 item passes/remediates; genuine failing item
   blocks; stale failing parent does not cover a child; missing audit still
   remediates.
7. Full suite passes; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` + `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
   describe the new Step 2 semantics.
data.title: Ship audit gate: share staleness logic with final validation (stop stale-verdict false blocks)

data.description:
## Goal

Bound the cost of in-gate audit remediation in the ship release so a backlog of
missing/stale audits cannot make a release run for hours or exhaust time/slot
budgets, and fail with an actionable offline-refresh instruction when the budget
is exhausted.

## Why

Both gates hardcode a 600000 ms per-item remediation timeout with no override and
no total budget. When a real audit takes >600s per item, every remediation is
recorded as `runner-failed` → blocking, and the release spends an unbounded
(worst case hours) time serially re-auditing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Per-item remediation timeout is configurable via env
   (`SHIP_AUDIT_REMEDIATION_TIMEOUT_MS`), defaulting to a value at least as large
   as a realistic audit phase (documented), applied in both gates.
2. A total remediation budget (wall-clock `SHIP_AUDIT_REMEDIATION_BUDGET_MS`
   and/or a max-items cap) bounds how many audits a single gating run attempts;
   exhaustion stops further attempts.
3. When the budget is exhausted, the gate returns blocking with a message that
   names the remaining items and instructs the operator to refresh audits
   offline (e.g. `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py batch`) rather than
   implying the work is "not ready to close".
4. A timeout (`ETIMEDOUT`) is reported distinctly from a genuine failing verdict
   in the blocked-item reason.
5. Unit tests cover: budget exhaustion stops attempts and blocks with the offline
   guidance; a single slow item respects the configured timeout; genuine
   fail-verdict still blocks without re-audit.
6. Full suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship audit gates: bound remediation cost and surface offline refresh guidance

data.description:
## Goal

Add a ship pre-flight that refreshes `in_review` audits *before* the release
gates run, so the release gating path becomes a cheap read-only audit sweep and
never spends the release window (and Code Freeze) serially re-auditing items.

## Why

Audit re-runs inside the release gate are inherently expensive and hold the
project-wide Code Freeze for their duration. The correct place for bulk
re-auditing is a supervised pre-flight step (using the audit runner's existing
`batch`/queue machinery), leaving the gate to verify, not to execute.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `run-release.js` supports a pre-flight audit-refresh action (e.g.
   `--refresh-audits`) that drives the audit runner for all `in_review` items
   missing/stale audits, outside the merge and outside the release gate budget.
2. When pre-flight is not requested, the gates remain read-only (no
   `audit_runner.py issue` execution) and block with the offline-refresh
   instruction from SA-…(child 2) when audits are missing/stale.
3. The Code Freeze marker is not set for a pre-flight-only run (or is scoped so
   the freeze covers only the merge, not the audit refresh).
4. Unit tests cover: pre-flight invocation path (mocked runner), gate left
   read-only when pre-flight is not requested, and Code Freeze scoping.
5. Full suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship: pre-flight audit refresh so release gating never runs long re-audits

data.description:
## Goal

Have the ship gates use the audit runner's persisted *content fingerprint*
(read-only) as the staleness signal, instead of the crude `auditedAt` vs
`updatedAt` time gate, so genuinely-unchanged items are not repeatedly queued for
re-audit when only a comment/status write bumped `updatedAt`.

## Why

`updatedAt` is bumped by comment/status writes (including the audit's own
persistence writes). The time-gate therefore labels good audits stale and feeds
them into the expensive remediation path. The audit runner already embeds an
`Audit content fingerprint:` line (description hash + Key Files + touched-file
state); consuming it read-only makes "stale" mean "audited content actually
changed".

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared helper extracts the content fingerprint from `wl audit-show`
   `rawOutput`/`summary` and compares it to the current item content fingerprint
   (or the runner's freshness contract) read-only.
2. When the fingerprint is unchanged, the gates classify the audit as fresh
   (not stale) even if `updatedAt` is newer.
3. When the fingerprint is absent (legacy audit), behaviour falls back to the
   existing time gate (no regression).
4. Unit tests cover: unchanged fingerprint → fresh despite newer `updatedAt`;
   changed fingerprint → stale; absent fingerprint → time-gate fallback.
5. Full suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint for staleness decisions

data.description:
## Goal

Improve release-gate operability: distinguish an audit-infrastructure failure
(timeout / concurrency / provider error) from a genuine "not ready to close"
verdict, and provide a narrow bypass that skips only in-gate remediation while
still verifying `readyToClose`.

## Why

Today the only escape hatch is `--skip-checks`, which bypasses every gate
(unmerged branches, critical items, worklog refs, producer review, final
validation). Operators facing a slow audit cannot skip just the expensive part.
And "remediation runner failed" is reported alongside genuine failing verdicts,
hiding the real cause.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit gates report a distinct reason/category for infra failures
   (timeout/ETIMEDOUT, concurrency limit, provider error) vs genuine failing
   verdicts, and the release output surfaces the category.
2. A narrow flag (e.g. `--skip-audit-remediation`) skips only the in-gate
   remediation attempts while still requiring `readyToClose===true` for every
   in-scope item; it is not forwarded to the merge script.
3. `--skip-checks` behaviour is unchanged.
4. Unit tests cover: infra-failure classification; narrow flag preserves the
   `readyToClose` check and blocks on a genuine failing verdict; flag is
   stripped from forwarded args.
5. Full suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship: distinguish audit-infra failures from genuine verdicts and add a narrow bypass
